description: A farmer has 200 acres of land on which he must process hay using either a windrower or hay harvester. For each acre of land, the windrower can process 10 kg of hay while the hay harvester can process 8 kg of hay. Per acre, the windrower produces 5 kg of methane gas and requires 2 kg of fuel. On the other hand, the hay harvester produces 3 kg of methane gas per acre and requires 1 kg of fuel. There are 300 kg of fuel available and the farmer can produce at most 800 kg of methane gas. For how many acres should each machine be used to maximize the amount of hay processed?

TotalAcres.definition: Total number of acres available for processing hay

NumMachines.definition: Number of different machine types available for processing hay

MethaneLimit.definition: Maximum allowable amount of methane gas production

HayProcessedPerAcre.definition: Amount of hay processed per acre by each machine type

MethaneProducedPerAcre.definition: Amount of methane gas produced per acre by each machine type

FuelRequiredPerAcre.definition: Amount of fuel required per acre by each machine type

objective.description: "Maximize the total amount of hay processed from the 200 acres using the available machines"

constraints.description: The total number of acres processed by the windrower and hay harvester must not exceed 200 acres
The total fuel used by both machines must not exceed 300 kg
The number of acres processed by each machine must be non-negative

AcresUsed.definition: Number of acres processed by each machine type
